findings.observation: SweepClient.start sets Probe.current=id. finish never clears it and there is no client clear command. The next distinct ID fails line31. /sweepqa dump/clear only changes server-process static state; it cannot clear a remote client/watch JVM. Integrated host may share the static and evade this, so integrated-only success does not validate the intended remote workflow.
findings.recommendation: Provide a client-local case lifecycle: preserve/flush late evidence, then explicitly permit a new unique ID and use a fresh per-case event buffer or filter saved records by case. Do not only remove the equality check: Probe.events is not cleared on remote start, so subsequent logs would retain earlier attack/end/wire events and break or pollute analysis.
findings.verification: Static call/state trace only; no game or reproduction run performed.

findings.observation: queue_empty_after_consumer uses all(...) without requiring any after-consumer event. For a negative, empty wire/geometry lists also satisfy absence. If Mixin configuration was not loaded, core QA command/event handlers can still record a cancelled attack and unchanged fixture HP while no probe-error is produced; this analyzer path can be mechanically green with no ReceiptProbe/VisualWireProbe/triangle instrumentation. defaultRequire=1 only enforces injections once that config is actually loaded.
findings.recommendation: Require recorded instrumentation readiness plus a nonempty before/after END coverage window. For negative visual absence, require the same installed probe/artifact identity and a successful positive calibration from that process/session, or an explicit loaded-hook receipt. Missing instrumentation should be TOOL_FAILURE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, never a successful absence result. HANDOFF already requires a positive first case; encode or explicitly link that dependency in each negative record.
findings.verification: Static empty-collection control flow, not a synthetic evidence execution.

findings.observation: The client accepts any alive LivingEntity ID within3 blocks. Server native-attack logging filters actor but not scoped target. Analyzer only counts one client attack and one server attack and never checks either target UUID against fixture.targets[0], nor checks client player UUID against fixture.actor or each record.case. A concrete static false-positive path is invulnerable mode armed on two QA cows while command attacks another nearby invulnerable entity: fixture HP stays unchanged, no dedicated cue/geometry appears, one attack is logged, and all current negative checks can pass without attacking the fixture.
findings.recommendation: Require current case on every consumed record, client actor UUID == server fixture actor, client/server attack target UUID == fixture primary UUID (and matching dimension), and matching mode/capture identity. Bind cancelled damage evidence to the expected source/targets; success receipt main should also match the primary fixture rather than only the actor.

positive_static_checks.observation: Read member tables from local SRG Jar. Custom target method/field names and AfterImages six-argument weapon descriptor match source injections; remap=false is appropriate for these mod-owned names. Java references to Minecraft APIs still require the planned reobf. No SRG QA artifact has been built/loaded by this review. The shared artifact is the recorded old production bundle; Receipt.level requires coordinator integration of the fixed four classes before running this QA.

Only explicit client command calls real MultiPlayerGameMode.attack followed by MAIN_HAND swing. No hand-built visual packet, FangtianSweep.begin/finish/tick, target.hurt, or setGameTime call appears in QA sources. Server creates noAI private cows and equips the test weapon, with full cooldown/range checks client-side; Native server event records are separate. This proves intended input path in source, not actual runtime packet transport.

ReceiptProbe reads queue/fields before and after the real consumer and does not alter receipt tick, flags or queue. Renderer probes are noncancelling injects, Shadow fields read-only. cancel-attack and cancel-damage mutate only matching actor/QA target events, invulnerable only QA targets; clear discards only stored QA-created targets. No original damage coefficient/cooldown/world time/health mutation of player. Reflection, list allocation and framebuffer readbacks can add timing overhead, so source nonmutation is not timing-neutrality or Forge-order proof.

evidence_boundaries.observation: actual-s2c-handle is logged at handle HEAD before valid()/reception-side/enqueued client renderer dispatch. It is a handler-entry observation, not by itself renderer acceptance. Positive geometry/pixel evidence is still required; no receipt record is a wire-send ACK.

Afterimage probe observes the weapon draw method entry and stack/matrix; it contains no actorUUID/packet sequence/start link. Wire mesh is actor-filtered, draw is only item-filtered. Same-frame geometry+draw proves co-occurrence of method calls, not that the original actor mesh is visible, unoccluded or correctly composed. Keep manual raw frames and private-single-attack context; do not infer GPU-visible old mesh solely from these logs.

Client explicitly selects FIRST_PERSON/THIRD_PERSON_BACK and logs actual views. Analyzer lists views but does not assert one requested view, verify both view coverage, or aggregate six controls/two positives. Coordinator must enforce the full plan across unique cases and inspect captures, not count two filenames as distinct views.

javac -proc:none checks Java typing, not Inject/Shadow application; local SRG symbol presence also does not prove load order, runtime transformed target, QA reobf or Mixin manifest loading. Positive preflight must cover server receipt and client wire/render hooks; missing events are tool failure.
